It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Dave thought bringing in Barnaby, his African Grey parrot, would be a charming way to boost morale. He didn’t realize that Barnaby had been listening to Dave’s late-night strategy calls with the CEO for three years.

The trouble started at 9:00 AM. Dave was on a hushed, confidential call with the CFO about the upcoming merger. "Look, if we shift the assets to the Cayman account by Friday, no one will know," Dave whispered, trying to sound professional.

Barnaby, perched on Dave’s shoulder, tilted his head. "No one will know," he squawked, perfectly mimicking Dave’s whisper.

Dave froze. He gently moved the bird to a cage in the corner. "Bad bird," he hissed.

At 10:00 AM, the CEO walked by. "Dave, how’s the merger prep going?"

Barnaby puffed his chest. "Shift the assets! Shift the assets!"

The CEO stopped. "Did you just say shift the assets?"

Dave sweated. "Uh, no. He’s... he’s a motivational bird. Very aggressive about logistics."

The CEO raised an eyebrow but walked away. Dave exhaled, only to hear Barnaby squawk, "Logistics! Logistics! And hide the receipts!"

By noon, the office was in chaos. Barnaby had learned the password to the server room ("Password123!") and was repeating it to anyone who looked at him. The IT director was having a stroke. The legal team was gathering in the breakroom, looking terrified.

Dave tried to cover his tracks. He bought a giant bag of birdseed and threw it at Barnaby, hoping to distract him. "Eat! Eat the evidence!" Dave yelled.

Barnaby ate a seed, then looked at the Legal Director. "Breach of contract! Breach of contract!"

The Legal Director dropped his coffee. "Dave! Is your bird confessing to fraud?"

"I’m working on it!" Dave shouted, grabbing a towel to drape over the cage. But Barnaby stuck his head out. "Dave is lying! Dave is lying! Also, I need a toothbrush!"
